receipts.first_text_witness: You're sitting at the dinner table with your college friends, the ones you haven't seen in 2 years because everyone's busy now, and somehow the conversation drifts, the way it always does after the second bottle of wine, toward money. Not in a serious way, just someone casually mentioning they refinanced, someone else saying they maxed out their Roth this year, and then one guy, the one who became an engineer and married someone in pharma, says, almost as an aside, that they're pretty close to the number. And you smile and nod because you know exactly what the number means, and you are not pretty close to it.
receipts.last_text_witness: written right now in the decision about this year's raise and whether you finally set up that Roth, in whether you run the real numbers instead of the comfortable ones. None of it feels important in the moment. All of it is. By watching this, you just did something most people never do. You looked the real numbers in the eye. Don't let that be the end of the story.
